title.narrative: Enhancing the protective environment of conflict-affected communities in Adamawa state through women-led mine action and GBV prevention

description.narrative: ltpgtThis proposal submission is for Thematic Envelope 1: Underfunded sector areas-based protection response. ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThrough an integrated mine action and gender-transformative protection response, the project will enhance the protective environment of vulnerable communities, especially vulnerable women and girls, affected by mine-related incidents. Based on the assumption that strengthening the female protective environment passes both by enhancing their inclusion in key community initiatives and addressing their specific protection risks, DRC and its implementing partner will pull together their specific expertise to 1) strengthen female leadership in key prevention initiatives related to mine incidents and Gender-Based Violence (GBV), and 2) provide a community-based protection response that directly prevents and mitigates mine action and Gender-Based Violence (GBV) risks, to which women and girls are particularly exposed. ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThe innovative approach that consists of integrating mine action and gender-specific concerns into the protection response will particularly materialize through the implementation of HMA and GBV-sensitive protection monitoring tools, specific capacity-building for female community members on mine action and GBV prevention, and the strong interaction between Psychosocial Support (PSS) and prevention activities on mine incidents and GBV. ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThe response will be implemented in Madagali, Michika, and Mubi North LGAs. DRC's Humanitarian Mine Action (HMA) team will implement the full mine action package of the response (Explosive Ordnance Risk Education - EORE) in all 3 LGAs, while its protection team will focus on Madagali and Michika where DRC already has protection safe spaces to implement its full protection response (structured and unstructured PSS, meetings, capacity-building, etc.). While the Center for Advocacy, Transparency, and Accountability Initiative (CATAI) will also contribute to DRC's response in Madagali and Michika, CATAI will complete it in Mubi North, where DRC does not have protection safe spaces. Particularly, CATAI will supervise the protection monitoring activities as well as the community focal points who will be trained to identify and refer individuals with protection concerns to the other specialized partners of the area. ltbrgtlt/pgt
